title: UNIT FIVE: POLITICS, ECONOMY, AND SOCIAL PROCESSES FROM THE EARLY SIXTEENTH TO THE END OF THE EIGHTEENTH CENTURIES
content:
ሰላም! ሰላም! ውዶቹ የEthioFresh ቤተሰቦቻችን! 🤗✨❤️ እንደምን ቆያችሁልን? ዛሬ ደግሞ የHistory of Ethiopia and the Horn (Hist. 1012) የምዕራፍ አምስት የመጀመሪያ ክፍል በሆነው Part 1 Tutorial ልንገናኝ በመቻላችን በጣም ደስ ብሎናል! ዛሬ በክፍል አንድ ክፍላችን ፦ በ16ኛው ክፍለ ዘመን በኢትዮጵያ ታሪክ ውስጥ ትልቅ ለውጥ ያመጣውን በክርስቲያኑ መንግሥትና በዐደል ሱልጣኔት መካከል የተደረገውን አሰቃቂ ጦርነት፣ የኢማም አሕመድ (ግራኝ) አመራርና ወታደራዊ ዘመቻዎች፣ የፖርቱጋልና የኦቶማን ቱርክ ጣልቃ ገብነት፣ እንዲሁም የካቶሊክ (የJesuit) ሚሲዮናውያን እንቅስቃሴና የሃይማኖት ክርክሮችን ከ5.1 እስከ 5.2 በዝርዝር፣ በምሳሌዎች፣ አዝናኝ የታሪክ ቀልዶችና ለፈተና 100% በሚያዘጋጁ Exam Hints አዘጋጅተንላችኋል። እስከ መጨረሻው አብራችሁን ተከታተሉ👇👇👇! ☕📖🚀

5.1. Conflict between the Christian Kingdom and the Sultanate of Adal, and the Aftermath

• Historical Context & Primary Causes: The first half of the sixteenth century was arguably the most turbulent period in the history of Ethiopia and the Horn. The main driver of chronic conflicts spanning over two centuries was control over long-distance trade routes passing through Zeila and the collection of tribute. Between 1529 and 1543, this trade rivalry escalated into a full-scale war of conquest.
• Rise of Imam Ahmed ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi:
- Origins & Early Career: Known in most Christian sources as "Gragn" (the left-handed), Imam Ahmed was likely born in Hubat (between Dire Dawa and Jijiga) around 1506. He began his military career under Garad Abun ibn Adash.
- Political Power Struggles: Garad Abun competed with Sultan Abu Bakr ibn Mohammed for power. After Garad Abun was killed in 1525, Imam Ahmed assumed leadership of the opposition, organized a formidable army, and eventually defeated and killed Sultan Abu Bakr in 1527.
• Environmental Pressures & Pastoralist Dynamics: The conflict was further fueled by environmental pressures facing Afar and Somali pastoralists. They were pushing towards Harar and the fertile highland plateau to secure pastureland due to population growth and overgrazing.
• Imam Ahmed's Leadership & Consolidation:
- Multi-Ethnic Coalition: Mobilized Afar, Somali, Argobba, Harla, Harari, and other groups under a common cause.
- Religious Unity & Salvation: With religious leaders' support, he brokered peace among fighting groups, redirecting their focus from inter-group warfare toward expansion into the Christian Kingdom, framing the war as a fight for salvation.
• Major Battles & Expansion Timeline:
- 1527: Launched offensives against frontier defenses, gaining control of Bali, Dawaro, Fatagar, Sidama, Hadiya, and Kambata.
- 1529 (Battle of Shimbra Kure): Emperor Lebne-Dengel assembled a vast force near present-day Mojo. Despite numerical superiority, the Christian army was routed due to logistical failures and lack of a unified strategy. Imam Ahmed's army succeeded due to high mobility, flexible tactics, and unified command.
- 1531–1535: Controlled Lasta, Begemedir, Dembiya, and Tigray. By 1535, Adal dominated most of the Christian territory.
- Administration & Del Wanbara: Established a bureaucracy using his own men and local recruits. His wife, Bati Del Wanbara (daughter of Mahfuz), accompanied him on military expeditions to avenge her father's death.
• Death of Lebne-Dengel & Foreign Interventions:
- 1540: Lebne-Dengel died as a fugitive; his son Gelawdewos (r. 1540–1599) succeeded him.
- 1541: Imam Ahmed received 200 Ottoman Turkish musketeers and 10 cannons.
- 1541: 400 Portuguese soldiers led by Christopher da Gama (son of Vasco da Gama) arrived with matchlocks following Lebne-Dengel's 1535 request to King João III.
- August 1542 (Battle of Wfla): Portuguese forces were defeated in southern Tigray; Christopher da Gama was captured and killed.
- February 1543 (Battle of Woyna Dega/Zantara): Emperor Gelawdewos defeated Adal forces east of Lake Tana, and Imam Ahmed was killed, marking the end of Adal territorial control.
• Post-Conflict Developments:
- Gelawdewos restored northern and central territories and reorganized chewa garrisons. In 1559, he was killed and beheaded by Emir Nur ibn al-Waazir Mujahid of Adal.
- Emperor Minas (r. 1559–1563) and Emperor Sartsa-Dengel (r. 1563–1598) neutralized Ottoman threats and regional rebellions led by Bahre Negash Yishaq.
• Consequences of the Conflict: Tremendous human and material destruction; weakening of both the Christian Kingdom and Muslim Sultanate, which paved the way for the Oromo population movement.

👉
1. የግጭቱ መንስኤና የኢማም አሕመድ አነሣሥ: በ16ኛው ክፍለ ዘመን የመጀመሪያው አጋማሽ በኢትዮጵያ ታሪክ ውስጥ ትልቅ ምስቅልቅል የታየበት ወቅት ነበር። የጦርነቱ ዋና መንስኤ የዘይላን የረጅም ርቀት ንግድ መስመር ለመቆጣጠርና ግብር ለመሰብሰብ የነበረው ፉክክር ነው። ኢማም አሕመድ ኢብን ኢብራሂም አል-ጋዚ (ግራኝ) በ1506 ገደማ በሁባት (በድሬዳዋና ጂጂጋ መካከል) ተወለደ። በ1527 ሱልጣን አቡ በክርን በመግደል የዐደልን ሥልጣን ያዘ።
2. የአካባቢና የህዝብ ተፅዕኖ: የአፋርና የሶማሌ አርብቶ አደሮች የመሬት ማነስና የከብት መብዛት (Overgrazing) ስላጋጠማቸው ወደ ደጋማው የክርስቲያን ግዛት መሬት ፍለጋ መንቀሳቀሳቸው ለጦርነቱ መፋፋም ምክንያት ሆነ።
3. የወታደራዊ ዘመቻዎችና ዋና ዋና ውጊያዎች:
- የሽምብራ ኩሬ ውጊያ (1529): በአሁኑ ሞጆ አቅራቢያ በተደረገው ውጊያ የአፄ ልብነ-ድንግል ግዙፍ ሠራዊት በወታደራዊ አመራር ድክመትና በስልት እጥረት በኢማም አሕመድ አነስተኛ ግን ፈጣን ሠራዊት ተሸነፈ።
- የግዛት መስፋፋት: እስከ 1535 ድረስ ኢማም አሕመድ ላስታ፣ በጌምድር፣ ደምቢያና ትግራይን ተቆጣጠረ። ባለቤቱ ባቲ ድል ወንበራ (የማሕፉዝ ልጅ) አባቷ በክርስቲያን መንግስት የተገደለባት የአባቷን ደም ለመመለስ አብራው እስከ ትግራይ ዘምታለች።
- የውጭ ሀገራት ጣልቃ ገብነት: ፖርቱጋሎች 400 ወታደሮችን በክርስቶፎሮ ዳ ጋማ መሪነት በ1541 ላኩ፤ በነሐሴ 1542 በወፍላ ውጊያ ተሸንፈው ዳ ጋማ ተገደለ። ኦቶማን ቱርኮች ደግሞ ለኢማም አሕመድ 200 የነፍስ ወከፍ ጠመንጃ ያዘጋጁ ወታደሮችንና 10 መድፎችን ሰጡ።
- የወይና ደጋ ውጊያ (የካቲት 1543): አፄ ገላውዴዎስ ከቀሩት ፖርቱጋሎች ጋር በመሆን በጣና ሀይቅ ምስራቅ በሚገኘው ዘንተራ (ወይና ደጋ) ኢማም አሕመድ ተገደለ፤ የዐደል የበላይነት አበቃ።
- የገላውዴዎስ ፍጻሜ: አፄ ገላውዴዎስ በ1559 በኤሚር ኑር ኢብን አል-ወዚር ሙጃሂድ ተገደለ።
4. የጦርነቱ አጠቃላይ ውጤት: የሰውና የንብረት እቅብታ ማጣት፣ የሁለቱም ኃይሎች መዳከም እና ለኦሮሞ ህዝቦች እንቅስቃሴ መንገድ የከፈተ ነበር።

💡 Exam Hints:
• Birthplace of Imam Ahmed: Hubat (between Dire Dawa and Jijiga).
• First Major Battle Victory for Imam Ahmed (1529): Battle of Shimbra Kure (near Mojo).
• Wife of Imam Ahmed who accompanied campaigns: Bati Del Wanbara.
• Leader of Portuguese Troops (1541): Christopher da Gama.
• Battle Where Imam Ahmed Was Killed (Feb 1543): Battle of Woyna Dega (Zantara).
• Adal Emir Who Killed Gelawdewos (1559): Emir Nur ibn al-Waazir Mujahid.

😂 የታሪክ ቀልድ: በወቅቱ የፖርቱጋልና የኦቶማን ቱርክ ጣልቃ ገብነት እኮ፤ አሁን ላይ ሁለት የአካባቢ ቡድኖች ሲጣሉ ውጭ ሀገር ያሉ ዘመዶቻቸው የገንዘብና የካርድ ክፍያ እንደመላክ ነው! ፖርቱጋል 400 ወታደር ስትልክ ቱርክ ደግሞ መድፍ ታጥቃ መጣች! 💣⚔️


5.2. Foreign Intervention and Religious Controversies

• Background & Imperial Motivations: Portuguese and Ottoman interventions reflected Red Sea and Indian Ocean geopolitics. Since Ethiopia lacked a navy, a direct military alliance with Portugal was limited. Monarchs sought Catholic alliance mainly to secure modern weaponry.
• Arrival of Jesuit Missionaries (1557):
- Theological Conflict: Jesuits taught the dual nature of Christ (separate divine and human natures), directly contradicting the Ethiopian Orthodox Church (EOC) Tewahedo doctrine (perfect human nature inseparable from the divine).
- Key Jesuit Figures: Joao Bermudez, Andreas de Oviedo, Pedro Paez, and Alfonso Mendez.
• Imperial Dynamics & Conversions:
- Gelawdewos: Debated missionaries and wrote Confession of Faith to defend EOC doctrine.
- Za-Dengel (r. 1603–1604): Secretly sympathetic to Catholicism; overthrown by Yaeqob.
- Susenyos (r. 1607–1632): Converted to Catholicism in 1612 with Pedro Paez's guidance and declared it the state religion in 1622 to secure foreign military aid against internal rebellions.
• Religious Reforms & Violent Backlash:
- Alfonso Mendez ordered re-consecration of EOC priests, re-baptism of masses, and prohibited circumcision, Ge'ez preaching, and Saturday Sabbath.
- Mandatory compliance with Latin Mass, Gregorian calendar, and eating pork triggered widespread civil war.
- June 1632 Battle: Massive peasant deaths led Susenyos to abdicate in favor of his son Fasilede.
• Fasiledes' Policy & Doctrinal Split:
- Closed-Door Policy: Restored EOC, expelled Jesuits, executed local converts (including Se'ela Kristos and Azazh Tino), and aligned with Ottoman Pashas at Suakin and Massawa to block Europeans.
- EOC Sectarian Splits (Zemene-Mesafint Peak):
1. Tewahedo: Hulet Lidet (Tigray & Lasta).
2. Qibat: Anointing (Gojjam).
3. Sost Lidet / Ya Tsega Lij: Three Births (Gonder & Shewa).
- Resolved at the Council of Boru Meda (1878) under Emperor Yohannes IV.

👉
1. የካቶሊክ (Jesuit) ሚሲዮናውያን መግባት: በ1557 ኢየሱሳውያን (Jesuits) ወደ ኢትዮጵያ ገቡ። የክርስቶስን ተፈጥሮ በተመለከተ የካቶሊክ ትምህርት (ሁለት ተፈጥሮ) ከኢትዮጵያ ኦርቶዶክስ ተዋሕዶ ትምህርት ጋር ተጋጨ።
2. የነገሥታቱ አቋም:
- ገላውዴዎስ: ከሚሲዮናውያን ጋር ተከራክሮ Confession of Faith የተባለውን የሃይማኖት መከላከያ ጽፏል።
- ሱሰንዮስ (1607–1632): በ1612 ወደ ካቶሊክ ተቀይሮ በ1622 ካቶሊክን የሀገር ሃይማኖት አደረገ።
3. የአልፎንሶ ሜንዴዝ አክራሪ ማሻሻያና ህዝባዊ አመፅ: ሜንዴዝ እንደገና ማጥመቅ፣ የሰንበትንና የግርዛትን መከልከል፣ በአማርኛ/ግዕዝ መስበክን ማገድ የመሳሰሉ ጠንካራ ውሳኔዎችን በማለፉ ሀገሪቱ ወደ የእርስ በእርስ ጦርነት ገባች። በሰኔ 1632 በሺዎች የሚቆጠሩ ገበሬዎች ካለቁ በኋላ ሱሰንዮስ ሥልጣኑን ለልጁ ፋሲለደስ አስረከበ።
4. የአፄ ፋሲለደስ የዝግ በር ፖሊሲ (Closed-Door Policy): ካቶሊኮችን አባረረ፤ የውጭ ሀገር አውሮፓውያን እንዳይገቡ ከኦቶማን ቱርክ ጋር ተስማማ።
5. በቤተክርስቲያን ውስጥ የተፈጠሩ የDoctrine ክፍፍሎች:
- ተዋሕዶ (ሁለት ልደት): በትግራይና ላስታ።
- ቅባት: በጎጃም።
- ሦስት ልደት (ፀጋ): በጎንደርና ሸዋ። (በ1878 በቦሩ ሜዳ ጉባኤ መፍትሔ አገኘ)።

💡 Exam Hints:
• Emperor Who Wrote "Confession of Faith": Gelawdewos.
• Emperor Who Declared Catholicism State Religion (1622): Susenyos.
• Spanish Jesuit Who Pushed Extreme Reforms: Alfonso Mendez.
• Emperor Who Introduced "Closed-Door Policy": Fasiledes.
